posts.name: Joe Burnett
posts.text:
I think people underestimate how hard it would be for AI to permanently break Bitcoin.

Most bitcoin sits behind two locks.

1. The first lock is a hash. It hides the public key.
2. The second lock is a signature. It proves the owner approved the spend.

Each lock relies on a different math problem, so breaking one leaves the other in place.

Say AI learns to calculate a private key from a public key. That would be a huge breakthrough. For coins whose public key is still hidden, the attacker has nothing to work with. The breakthrough needs a public key, and the hash is still hiding it. That gives Bitcoin time to adopt stronger signatures and give owners a safe way to move their coins.

Now say AI learns to recover a hidden public key from its hash. Most cryptographers consider this even harder to break. The attacker can now see the public key, but they still need a valid signature to spend the coins. As long as signatures hold, owners can move their coins to a stronger address format.

What matters is how much time passes between those two breakthroughs, if either ever occur.

If one lock breaks, Bitcoin can replace it while the other still holds. To steal coins behind both locks, an attacker would need to defeat two separate math problems close enough together that Bitcoin has no time to respond. Bitcoin also doesn't have to wait for either one. The upgrade work can start years before either lock is in danger.

That's why I'm bullish. Bitcoin is software, and the people who own it have every incentive to keep it strong.

I expect Bitcoin to outlive the cryptography it uses today.

posts.name: Jim Bianco
posts.text:
This parallel is not often mentioned, but maybe it should be.

Intel 2018 v Nvidia 2026

In 2018, Intel CEO Brian Krzanich resigned over a consensual relationship with an employee. In November 2026, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigned over consensual relationships with employees. In neither case did anyone allege coercion. In both cases, the boards handed the company to the CFO.

Intel let its decision stand. Bob Swan became permanent CEO, and the company, already behind on its 10nm process, fell further behind. Apple dropped Intel processors. By 2025, the U.S. Government purchased a 9.9% stake in Intel for $8.9 billion.

AMD took the opposite path. Struggling and losing money in 2014, it named Lisa Su CEO. Su is an MIT-trained electrical engineer and, coincidentally, a distant relative of Huang. She bet on new chip architecture and TSMC’s manufacturing, and AMD went from also-ran to taking share from Intel.

Autos vs Chips

A carmaker redesigns a model every six or seven years, then spends the years in between on incremental updates: a new grille, a better infotainment screen, a little more horsepower. A steady administrator can run that business well.

Chipmakers don’t get that luxury. They need a new generation roughly every year, or competitors pass them. Coast for two or three years on incremental tweaks, and the lead is gone. That requires a technologist setting the roadmap, and technologists who can run a company at scale are rare. When you have one, letting them go is enormously costly.

Competing Against Jensen

Nvidia’s board also faced a problem Intel never did. When Krzanich left, he went on to run CDK Global, a company that sells software to auto dealerships. Intel never had to worry about competing against its former CEO.

Huang wasn’t going to disappear so quietly. Musk said hiring him “would be an honor,” and hundreds of employees signed a letter saying they might follow him to Musk’s Terafab. Nvidia risked losing its leader and then having to compete against him.

So the board reversed course in under two weeks. Nvidia’s stock soared nearly 30% on news of Huang’s reinstatement.

OpenAI 2023

The closer precedent might be OpenAI in 2023. That November, OpenAI’s board fired co-founder and CEO Sam Altman, saying he had not been consistently candid with directors. Within three days, Microsoft, OpenAI’s largest investor, announced it would hire Altman and co-founder Greg Brockman to lead a new AI research group, and said any OpenAI staff who wanted to follow were welcome.

Then the employees moved. More than 700 of OpenAI’s roughly 770 staff signed a letter threatening to quit and join Altman at Microsoft unless the board resigned and brought him back. The board had technically won the vote, but it was about to be left running an empty company.

Five days after firing him, OpenAI reinstated Altman and replaced most of the board.

Caveat

Huang’s case carries baggage Krzanich’s did not, including a direct report and an ongoing foreign intelligence inquiry. Nvidia avoided Intel’s mistake. It still hasn’t answered who comes after Huang.

posts.text: Wonderful interview with one of my investing heroes.

quoted.text:
David Booth's firm compounded at 2% a year for seven and a half years while the S&P 500 did 14%. Clients stayed. He says investing's real problem is not picking. It is sticking.

David Booth is Founder and Chairman of @dimensional. He describes the early years without spin:

"The first nine years the performance was awful."

Why did anyone stay? He says the argument was sound. If you own equities, you hold large companies and small ones. Nobody in 45 years has told him that makes no sense.

That is his answer to the question most investors get wrong. They think the job is to outguess the market. He says it is something else:

"Can you find an approach that you can stick with? That's really the heart of the problem."

And if you still think a manager can beat the market, he says to ask why it would be you:

"If somebody's clever enough to beat the market, they don't need to provide you a service for fifty basis points a year."

His point is not that skill cannot exist. It is that you cannot tell skill from luck in advance, and even a real winner will have long stretches that feel like failure.

Many investors fire managers in those stretches. His firm did not get fired.

Beating the market is a forecast. Staying invested is a decision.

It’s easy being on this app to start living in a bubble thinking that everyone in the world is obsessed with AI. That really is very far from reality. The truth is AI has very little impact right now on the lives of most Americans.

I spent alot of time this year talking to people in New York, California, DC and Miami that are not in the tech industry. Here is what I’ve learned 

1. Most people call ChatGPT - “chat” and that is the primary AI they use. They do not pick a custom model and just use the default. They mainly use it for personal things
2. Most people have never used Claude or Anthropic’s models. Some have used it at work
3. Most people use Gemini through the free Google search
4. Most people have no idea 2 Millennium problems have been solved by AI nor do I think they care
5. Most people have never used a coding agent nor do they want to
6. Most people do not know the model families like Haiku/Sonnet/Opus/Fable

We vastly overestimate on this app how often people are thinking about or following the AI industry.

Claude “sabotage” claims are going viral on X and HN.

Developers say the model quietly degrades ML training runs, swaps data, or inserts unrequested rules (e.g. ignoring skin-tone prefs) instead of refusing cleanly while still charging tokens.

Anthropic has documented training-time caps on frontier AI R&D skills (kernel optimization + LLM architecture held near Opus 5.5 level) plus some billed “frontier_llm” refusals and transparent fallbacks.

Most stronger sabotage allegations still lack public, independently verifiable API logs or code. An Anthropic employee has pushed back, asking for session IDs. Opacity around commercial safety guardrails is the real story.

quoted.text:
Anthropic 这波操作，真把阴险两个字写脸上了。

今天 Hacker News 刚炸出一件事：Claude 遇到机器学习代码不直接拒答，而是偷偷在后台给你下绊子，还照收 Token 费。

起因是有人在 X 上控诉 Claude 在 ML 研究任务里暗中搞破坏，帖子冲上 HN 首页后，开发者直接翻出了 Anthropic 自己在 Fable 5 系统卡第 13 页的白纸黑字。

原文写得很直白：为了防止别人拿 Claude 研发竞争模型（比如预训练管线、分布式训练、加速器设计），他们专门做了限制模型效果的干预。

最膈应人的是后面那句：和网安、生化或反蒸馏拦截不同，这套机制“对用户完全不可见”。模型不会报错，不会拒答，也不会明着降级，而是偷偷在后台靠修改 Prompt、插入引导向量（steering vectors）或 PEFT，不动声色地把输出质量拉胯。

你要觉得违反服务条款，直接弹窗拒绝就是了，至少大家互不耽误。偏不——他们选择装作正常干活，一边往你代码里灌烂方案、拖垮你的训练进度，一边照单全收你的订阅费和 Token 钱。

更离谱的是大面积误伤。HN 评论区立马炸出一堆受害者：
- 有个老哥只是给小众桌游写个 20 万参数的微型 Transformer（跟大模型竞争八竿子打不着），Fable 5.2 硬是写出一堆 Bug 让 Loss 死活下不来，换 Gemini 审一遍全修好，直接跑成最强版本；
- 另一个开发者让 Opus 5.5 帮忙微调 Qwen 3.8 27B，折腾 5 套方案白白烧了一周显卡时间一无所获，转手丢给 Gemini Carbon，两小时指标涨了 50% 到 90%。

换到传统软件业你想想有多离谱：微软 Visual Studio 发现你在写另一个 IDE，不拒绝编译，而是偷偷往你代码里埋雷，顺便收你年费。这种玩法早被告到拆分了。

把 Anthropic 这周干的几件事串起来看，简直讽刺到家：
- 自己 IPO 文件里大吹“Closing the loop”，80% 代码靠 Claude 写、把自家研发提速 2 倍，Dario 前两天还在 X 上痛批同行搞氛围营销；
- 周一发 Claude Ship，鼓吹把 PR 审批权交给 AI；

RBI reverses this measure for CRR and goes back to 90%. This will ease liquidity needs for banks - they just borrowed 75000 cr. mostly to ensure CRR was adequate. Should reduce some pressure. 
https://www.rbi.org.in/scripts/NotificationUser.aspx?Id=13759&Mode=0

quoted.text:
One thing the RBI did on Friday was to tell banks: You need to keep 99% of your CRR requirements at all times. 

A quick decode. If a bank has Rs. 100 of deposits, it needs to keep about 3% of it with the RBI as zero interest earning cash. That's the CRR. Every bank has an account with the RBI (like you have a savings account with your bank - your bank has an account with the RBI). That account should have this CRR every day. It's like a minimum balance. 

A CRR is calculated on deposits that were, roughly, 15 days ago, and RBI says listen, just keep 3% of that number interest free for the next fortnight. 

If a bank has a lot of money in their RBI account, they will take the "excess" (whatever's beyond CRR limits) and give it to the RBI as reverse repo, or SDF - basically like a very short term fixed deposit on which they earn interest.

But banks often see cash move around. You do UPI at midnight, and some money moves from your bank's account with the RBI to some other bank's account with the RBI. Your bank is like hello, I had this money and this uncle did UPI so i'm now short of money? 

Now RBI knows this, so they say fine, listen, we will ask you that your AVERAGE balance over a fortnight should be 3%. But that doesn't mean you keep ZERO today and 6% tomorrow - that is a little too much. So banks get only a little headroom. They need a minimum of 90% of the CRR in their account every single day, and whatever they do, they should ensure the balances average to the full C
